# Vixely

> A browser-based editor for images, video, GIFs, audio and subtitles. Every
> operation runs locally through WebCodecs and WebGL; no file is ever uploaded,
> there is no backend and no database.

Vixely replaces several desktop tools with one web interface. It serves both the
person converting a PNG to WebP in three seconds and the person re-encoding a
film to HEVC across four audio tracks and two styled subtitle tracks.

## Routes

- /: overview of the five editors.
- /tools/image: convert, crop, resize, colour-correct, add text layers.
- /tools/video: frame-accurate trimming, track management, filters, re-encoding.
- /tools/gif: frame timeline, delays, palette quantisation, conversion.
- /tools/audio: cut, rearrange, normalise (EBU R128), equalise, convert.
- /tools/subtitles: edit cues, styles and headers for SRT, WebVTT, ASS and PGS.

## Formats

- Images in: PNG, JPEG, WebP, AVIF, GIF, BMP, SVG, ICO. Out: PNG, JPEG, WebP, AVIF.
- Video containers: MP4, MOV, MKV, WebM, MPEG-TS. Codecs: H.264, HEVC, VP8, VP9, AV1, ProRes.
- Audio codecs: AAC, Opus, MP3, Vorbis, FLAC, AC-3, E-AC-3, DTS, PCM.
- Subtitles: SRT, WebVTT, ASS/SSA and PGS, embedded in Matroska or as sidecar files.

## Constraints worth knowing

- Nothing is uploaded. There is no API to call and no account to create.
- Streaming writes to disk require a Chromium browser; elsewhere the output file
  is assembled in memory and very large exports are refused up front.
- Firefox on Android has no WebCodecs support and is told so explicitly.
- ASS and PGS subtitles can only be embedded in Matroska: MP4 standardises
  neither.
